note:
Import record for "Charged Dinner", malvora.'s homebrew script, written from its Klutzbanana page: the game data (ability, team, night order and night reminders, reminder tokens, setup, special) from the script's own JSON, and the almanac prose (flavour line, lede, summary, examples, how to run, storyteller notes) from each character's almanac on the same page. Nothing was written that the source does not say. Notes:
- Five names are already used by other creators here (Doctor, Nightmare, Prosecutor, Saboteur, Sleuth), so those take a -charged-dinner URL suffix in the wiki's existing duplicate style. The other 21 keep their plain slug.
- Klutzbanana states almanac prose as one markdown blob. It is split into the wiki's lede / summary / examples / how-to-run fields; its fenced storyteller notes become Tips & Tricks entries; its **emphasis** markers are dropped and its :char[Name]{name=Name} links become plain names, because a character field is plain text and only [[TOKEN]] means anything to render.js. No words are changed.
- Night order numbers are the author's own. Klutzbanana states them as positions within this script (other nights run 5 to 23), not on the official global scale the wiki's night-order picker uses, so they sort this script exactly as intended but do not interleave correctly with official characters in a mixed script.
- Every character ships two icons, its own and the alignment-flipped one, stored as art and artAlt. The Philanthropist ships three (two-tone, good, evil): the two-tone icon is the traveller's own art and the evil one takes the alternate slot. All of them go through the site's own 591x591 resize, the same transform as assets/art-normalize.js.
- The script is Starlight. There is no collection for the set: the 26 character pages carry no tags, because the source has none, so they are Partial (assets/classify.js) and are reachable from the script page, their creator page and a direct link rather than from browsing. A script's Starlight is its own; only a collection lends the status to its members (applyCollectionStarlight in worker.js).
- jsonId carries Klutzbanana's own ids (patrolman_charged_dinner and friends), so a script built here exports the same ids as the source JSON.
- The script's almanac introduction is split the way the wiki's script page is shaped: the narrative into Synopsis, the Overview paragraph into Gameplay, and the two "When playing Charged Dinner..." halves into Playing Good and Playing Evil.

script.name: Charged Dinner
script.author: malvora.
script.synopsis:
Heavy rain hammers steadily against the windows of Abercroft Manor. The cypresses shake violently amidst the howling winds, and the massive iron gate that guards the premises creaks and rattles in an erratic rhythm. Solely kept at bay by a few lonely lanterns, a deep, engulfing darkness creeps its way ever closer towards the manor doors.

Inside, however, earthly worries are cast aside, guests frolic merrily amongst one another, the highest members of high society are all gathered here, in the presence of His Lordship himself. It is only when lightning strikes at the most inopportune of moments and the darkness closes in on the gathered crowd that the mood starts to shift. And when the first dead body makes its appearance on the premises, all pretense of class crumbles, and all in attendance are more than happy to point fingers and shift blame.

The air is prickling with hidden resentment (and, quite possibly, knives), and one thing is clear above all: This will be a...

Charged Dinner.
script.gameplay: Charged Dinner is a vanilla-style homebrew script that runs in two intermingling halves - one focused on nominations, one focused on how many deaths occur at night - with the intent of increasing the tension of both the day and night phase. Nominations gain purpose in addition to deciding the day's execution, leading to an ever-raging battle between using them to gather information and using them to further the good team's main goal: finding and executing the Demon.
script.strategyGood:
Good players will need to use nominations to their advantage to make the most out of the information they get. The town square is littered with dangerous traps, and the Demons that haunt the mansion require different approaches to be dealt with. The Lady poisons everyone she nominates, meaning those who nominate frequently might often be your most dangerous opponents. The Guvna turns a good player into their scapegoat, so town needs be careful about a player who seems not to be fitting in. The Mansel can make the first player to nominate them turn evil, which means pointing fingers is a difficult decision that must be considered twice. Lastly, the Noster can kill Outsiders or even their Minions to unleash a killing spree, which means both that Outsiders should be careful about revealing who they are and that the most trustworthy players might very well be those who are still alive.

Each Outsider is a trap for the good team to step into. They throw a wrench into smooth proceedings by ending games earlier than expected, making players drunk, or causing deaths at inopportune moments.
script.strategyEvil: Evil players will want to dismantle the good team's potent threats as quickly as possible. Charged Dinner's Minions are loud and make themselves known pretty quickly - which is why a well-timed switch into a different Minion via the Snob might be what saves the evil team's hide. The Nightmare accelerates the game, but does so at the cost of giving the good team even more information. The Curfew on the other hand limits the amount of nominations players can make and wrests control over executions away from town. Similarly, the Saboteur can make it so different players get executed than town actually wants. Evil can do great amounts of damage by using up town's valuable resources and sowing mistrust wherever they can. However, just as it is tempting for good players to nominate recklessly in spite of the dangers, the evil team should be careful about nominating too often, should they wish to avoid suspicion befalling them...

characters.name: Patrolman
characters.ability: You & an evil player start knowing a good player & their character.
characters.lede: The Patrolman knows a good player - but their evil "partner" knows them too.
summaryBullets: On the first night, the both the Patrolman and an evil player learn the identity of a good player.
Both players must learn the same player and the same character. The evil player cannot get different information.
If the Patrolman is drunk or poisoned, they learn arbitrary info and no evil player learns anything.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Patrolman. Point at a good player and show the Patrolman their character token. Put the Patrolman to sleep. Then, wake an evil player. Point at the same good player and show the evil player the same character token. Put the evil player to sleep.
examples: The Patrolman and the Nightmare learn that Anna is the Chaperone. During the day, both claim that they are the Patrolman and reveal to Anna that they know who she is.

The Patrolman and the Guvna learn that James is the Doctor. During the day, the Guvna claims to be the Socialite and nominates one of the James' neighbors. The next day, they claim to have seen the Doctor character token.
characters.quote: Out with it! Where were you on the night of the 15th and why did you not open your bakery at the request of one of our city's finest when he happened to be peckish?
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Patrolman a good player and their character token. Then, wake an evil player and show them that same player and their character token.

characters.name: Inquisitor
characters.ability: You start knowing a Minion and a Demon character, exactly 1 of which is in play.
characters.lede: The Inquisitor knows that only one of a specific Minion and Demon is in play.
summaryBullets: On the first night, the Inquisitor learns a Minion and a Demon character, of which only one is assigned to a player.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Inquisitor. Show the Inquisitor the character token of a Demon and a Minion, of which only one is in play. Put the Inquisitor to sleep.
examples: The Demon is the Mansel, and their Minions are the Curfew and the Saboteur. The Inquisitor learns the Mansel and the Nightmare.
The Demon is the Guvna and their Minion is the Snob. The Storyteller decides to let the Snob's neighbor register as the Nightmare. The Inquisitor learns the Lady and the Nightmare.
characters.quote: Rest easy, my wayward little lamb. Your sins may weigh heavy upon your conscience, but in His eyes, they are but flies to be purged in the eternal flames of hell.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the character tokens of a Minion and a Demon, exactly one of which is in play.

characters.name: Occultist
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: if you died today or tonight, learn if any chosen player is the Demon.
characters.lede: When the Occultist dies, they learn if they chose a Demon while alive.
summaryBullets: Each night, the Occultist chooses a player. If they then die, they learn if there was a Demon among their choices.

The Occultist's choices are evaluated correctly even if they are drunk or poisoned. A drunk Occultist choosing the Demon still gets the "Demon chosen" reminder placed beside them. If they die and wake to learn their information while drunk or poisoned, the Storyteller may lie to them as usual.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Occultist. The Occultist points at any player. If the chosen player is a Demon, mark the Occultist with the DEMON CHOSEN reminder. Put the Occultist to sleep.
If the Occultist died today or tonight, wake them at their point in the night order and nod your head yes if they are marked with the DEMON CHOSEN reminder or shake your head no if they aren't.
examples: The Occultist chose the Countess, the Socialite and the Saboteur, then died. They learn a "no".
The Occultist chose the Guvna, the Maiden and the Doctor. Today, the Maiden was executed and died, making all Townsfolk drunk. Tonight, the Guvna kills the Occultist. They learn a "no".
characters.quote: Oh yes, I can see it... I can see it... the number 7... a cyclone... a doll with no head... you will soar to great heights...
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Occultist points at a player. If they are the Demon, mark the Occultist with the DEMON CHOSEN reminder.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Occultist died and the Occultist is marked with the DEMON CHOSEN reminder, nod your head yes. If they didn't die, the Occultist points at a player. If they are the Demon, mark the Occultist with the DEMON CHOSEN reminder.

characters.name: Merrymaker
characters.ability: Each day, publicly choose up to 3 players (not yourself): if all are good, they can't die tonight.
characters.lede: The Merrymaker gets to keep people alive - as long as they don't try to protect an evil player.
summaryBullets: Each day, the Merrymaker may publicly name up to 3 players (not themself) to make merry with. If all chosen players are good, none of them can die that night. If even one of them is evil, they are all vulnerable.

Mumbled names, whispers, or names that someone cannot hear don’t count. Like the Slayer’s ability, the Storyteller and every player must be able to hear and understand the Merrymaker and be aware that the Merrymaker is using their ability in order for the Storyteller to judge what happens next.
If the Merrymaker made merry with only good players during the day while drunk or poisoned, but is sober and healthy when their ability triggers that night, the chosen players are still protected.
howToRun: Each day, if the Merrymaker names only good players to protect, put the Merrymaker's CANNOT DIE reminders next to every player who will be protected that night.
examples: During the day, the Merrymaker says, "I am the Merrymaker. I would like to protect Anna, Beatrice and Clara." Anna, Beatrice and Clara are all good. That night, all three cannot die.
The Merrymaker makes merry with two people. One of them is evil. That night, the Demon targets one of the named people: they die.
The Merrymaker makes merry with both their neighbors. They are good. That night, the Demon kills the Merrymaker. Immediately after, the Nightmare kills one of the Merrymaker's neighbors.
characters.quote: Ohh, Jerry... Hm? Nooo, I'm not having a party, who told you that? Allison? Yeah, no, she must have meant some other party, one that isn't happening... here.
characters.creator: malvora.

characters.name: Sleuth
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a character (not a Demon): learn that it is 1 of 2 players. If not in play, learn arbitrary info.
characters.lede: The Sleuth can find characters in the town square.
summaryBullets: Once per game, during the night phase, the Sleuth gets to choose a character to learn where on the town square that character might be.
If the character they choose is not in play, the Sleuth learns any two players. This happens even if another character's ability were to cause them to learn "true" information.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Sleuth. The Sleuth may point at a character on their character sheet. If the chosen character is in play, point at 2 players, 1 of which is that character. If it isn't, point at 2 players of your choosing. Put the Sleuth to sleep.
If the Sleuth used their ability, put the NO ABILITY reminder next to the Sleuth and don't wake them any following nights.
examples: The Sleuth chooses the Occultist. The Occultist is in play. The Storyteller points to the Occultist and the Paranoiac.
The Sleuth chooses the Curfew. They are not in play. The Storyteller points to the Anomaly and the Maiden.
characters.quote: Hmm... This dirt tells me a lot about our killer. Seems like I've finally got some... dirt on him! HA! I'm a genius!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Sleuth may choose a non-Demon character. If they do, point at two players, 1 of which is that character. If the character is not in play, point at 2 players.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Sleuth has not yet used their ability, the Sleuth may choose a non-Demon character. If they do, point at two players, 1 of which is that character. If the character is not in play, point at 2 players.

characters.name: Groundskeeper
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a dead player: you learn their alignment.
characters.lede: The Groundskeeper discovers the alignment of a dead player.
summaryBullets: Once per game, during the night phase, the Groundskeeper gets to choose a dead player to learn whether they are good or evil.
The Groundskeeper may only choose dead players. If they choose an alive player, prompt them to choose again.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Groundskeeper. The Groundskeeper may point at a player. Show the appropriate thumb signal. Put the Groundskeeper to sleep.
If the Groundskeeper used their ability, put the NO ABILITY reminder next to the Groundskeeper and don't wake them any following nights.
examples: The Groundskeeper chooses the dead Occultist. The Storyteller shows a thumbs up.
The Groundskeeper chooses the dead Guvna-poisoned Patrolman. The Storyteller shows a thumbs down.
characters.quote: I didna like dat dere fella. Yuge pain in da rear. Always seem'd a lil off if ye ask me.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Groundskeeper has not yet used their ability, the Groundskeeper may choose a dead player. If they do, give a thumb signal.

characters.name: Doctor
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose that a good player who would die tonight does not. You cannot save yourself this way.
characters.lede: The Doctor can save players from dying at the last second.
summaryBullets: Once per game, during the night phase (not the first), the Doctor can choose to save a good player, and if they do, a good player that would die for any reason does not.
The Doctor can save any good player, no matter how they die.
The Doctor's ability must save a good player if it can. If there is no valid player to save that night, no player is saved.
Once the Doctor has used their ability, stop waking them.
The Doctor cannot save themselves.
A player turned evil by the Mansel cannot be saved.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Doctor. Ask if they want to use their ability. If they do, mark them with the NIGHT SHIFT reminder. Put the Doctor to sleep. If they used their ability, at any point in the night, mark a good player that would die with the SAVED reminder and don't place any DEAD reminders. Replace the NIGHT SHIFT reminder with the NO ABILITY reminder.
examples: The Doctor chooses to use their ability. That night, the Demon kills the Paranoiac who redirects the kill into the Saboteur and the Countess kills a player. The player killed by the Countess does not die.
The Doctor chooses to use their ability. The Demon chooses a player protected by the Merrymaker and the Countess kills the Snob. No one is saved by the Doctor's ability.
characters.quote: Show me where it hurts. Mhm. Mhm. Yes, considering all your symptoms, my professional medical diagnosis is that something bit off half your face.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Doctor has not yet used their ability, the Doctor may choose to use their ability.

characters.name: Countess
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, you may choose to kill the player you nominated today. A killed Demon lives, but is drunk until dusk.
characters.lede: The Countess can kill one player that she nominated the day before or keep the Demon from killing for a night.
summaryBullets: If the Countess nominated during the day, that night, she may kill the player she nominated. She can only do this once per game, and if the player she hits is the Demon, they don't die, but rather become drunk until dusk the next day.
If the Countess didn't nominate today, they are not woken.
howToRun: If the Countess nominates, mark that player with the NOMINEE reminder. That night, wake them and ask them if they want to use their ability. If they do, mark the player they nominated with the DEAD reminder, or, if they're the Demon, with the DRUNK reminder. Put the Countess to sleep.
examples: The Countess didn't nominate today. Tonight, she doesn't wake.
The Countess nominated the Socialite today. Tonight, she chooses to kill them. They die.

The Countess nominated the Lady today. Tonight, she chooses to kill them. The Lady lives but is drunk. The Prosecutor was nominated by the Lady today, but because the Lady is drunk, they receive healthy info tonight.
characters.quote: My husband? What a lovely fellow he was, always reliable. Reliable in marriage, reliable in drink... Such a shame that paint thinner and hard liquor look so much alike.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Countess nominated today, she may choose to use her ability.

characters.name: Anomaly
characters.ability: You think you are a Demon bluff, but you are not. A good player starts knowing you are 1 of 2 players.
characters.lede: The Anomaly player thinks that they are a good character, and has no idea that they are actually the Anomaly. A good player knows to look out for the Anomaly.
summaryBullets: During setup, the Anomaly's token does not go in the bag. Instead, a good character token goes in the bag, and the player who draws that token is secretly the Anomaly for the whole game. The Storyteller knows. The player does not.

The Anomaly has no ability. Whenever their ability would affect the game in some way, it doesn't. However, the Storyteller pretends that the player is the character they think they are. If that character would wake at night, the Anomaly wakes to act as if they are that character. If that character would gain information, the Storyteller may give them false information instead - and the Storyteller is encouraged to do so.
Any good player starts the game knowing that the Anomaly is 1 of 2 players. The Anomaly can also learn this themselves..
The token the Anomaly pulls must then also be shown to the Demon as part of the three characters they see during the first night.
howToRun: While setting up the game, before putting character tokens in the bag, remove the Anomaly token and add a Townsfolk or Outsider character token. Add the Anomaly's IS THE ANOMALY reminder token to the Grimoire. Put the swapped character token in the bag, not the Anomaly character token.

While preparing the first night, put the Anomaly's IS THE ANOMALY reminder token by any good character token, changing that player's character to the Anomaly. They are now a Townsfolk, and do not have the ability of their supposed character. (But they think they do.)
During the first night, wake a good player (marked with the KNOWS reminder) and show them the Anomaly token. Point to two players, one of which is the Anomaly. Put the good player to sleep.

During the game, act as if the Anomaly is actually this character. (If that character would wake to act at night, the Anomaly wakes to act. If their ability would give them information, you can give false information to them if you wish. See "Drunkenness and Poisoning" in the rulebook.)
examples: The Anomaly thinks they are the Countess. The Demon is shown that the Groundskeeper, the Maiden and the Countess are not in play.
The Anomaly thinks they are the Paranoiac. The Demon attacks them in the night. They die.
The Anomaly thinks they are the Veteran. The Socialite learns that either the Anomaly or the Curfew is the Anomaly.
tips: If the Anomaly thinks they are an Outsider, the Outsider count must still be satisfied without counting the Anomaly (i.e. there has to be an additional Outsider in play).
characters.quote: #ERROR#: DATA NOT FOUND. ASSIGNING BACKUP VALUE.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake a good player and show them the THIS CHARACTER IS IN PLAY and Anomaly tokens. Point to 2 players, 1 of which is the Anomaly.

characters.name: Prosecutor
characters.ability: If you nominated today, tonight, learn a player of the nominee's alignment.
characters.lede: The Prosecutor can find witnesses for the people they accuse.
summaryBullets: If the Prosecutor nominated today, they learn a player of the nominee's alignment tonight.
Which player they are shown is entirely up to the Storyteller's discretion.
If the Prosecutor didn't nominate today, they are not woken.
howToRun: If the Prosecutor nominates, mark that player with the NOMINEE reminder. That night, wake them and show them a player of the same alignment as the marked player. Put the Prosecutor to sleep.
examples: Today, the Prosecutor nominated the Anomaly. Tonight, the Storyteller points to the Patrolman.
Today, the Prosecutor didn't nominate. Tonight, they don't wake.
Today, the Prosecutor nominated the Guvna. Tonight, the Storyteller points to the Guvna-poisoned Sleuth.
characters.quote: Your Honor! It is a gross indignity to have this witness brought before my stand! Ravens cannot be made to give sworn testimony!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Prosecutor nominated today, show them a player of the same alignment as the player they nominated.

characters.name: Socialite
characters.ability: If you nominated today, tonight, learn the character of one of the nominee's neighbors (skipping you).
characters.lede: The Socialite can learn the characters of the players that neighbor the player they nominate.
summaryBullets: If the Socialite nominated today, they learn the character of one of the nominee's neighbors tonight.
Which neighbor's character they learn is entirely up to the storyteller's discretion.

If the Socialite nominated one of their own neighbors, they cannot learn themselves that night. Instead, they are skipped over and can learn their other neighbor's character (Learnable-Nominee-Socialite-Learnable).
If the Socialite didn't nominate today, they are not woken.
howToRun: If the Socialite nominates, mark that player with the NOMINEE reminder. That night, wake them and show them the character token of one of their neighbors. Put the Socialite to sleep.
examples: The Socialite nominated a player who neighbors the Merrymaker and the Countess. That night, they learn the Countess.

The Socialite nominates a player who neighbors the Noster and the Spinster. They learn the Spinster. The following day, they nominate a player that neighbors the Noster and the Prosecutor. They learn the Prosecutor.
The Socialite neighbors the Lady and the Patrolman. They nominate the Lady, who also neighbors the Veteran. That night, they learn the Patrolman.
tips: The Socialite is a very powerful character. Try to avoid confirming a player too quickly and cast doubt on players at the right moments instead of at every turn.
characters.quote: Oh, you simply must tell me about Agatha! No! She did what?! Oh my, wait 'till Evelyn hears of this. Evelyn! Evelyn, darling, wait!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Socialite nominated today, show them the character of one of the neighbors of the player they nominated.

characters.name: Chaperone
characters.ability: If only good players nominated today, tonight, a good player learns you are the Chaperone.
characters.lede: The Chaperone reveals themselves to a player if only good players nominated.
summaryBullets: If only good players nominated during the day, that night, a good player learns the player who has the Chaperone token.
If an evil player nominated today, no one learns who the Chaperone is that night.
If a good player who nominated today turns evil before the Chaperone's turn in the night order, they count as an evil player for the purposes of the Chaperone ability.
howToRun: During the day, if an evil player nominates, mark the Chaperone with the EVIL NOMINATED reminder. That night, if the Chaperone is not marked with the EVIL NOMINATED reminder, wake a good player, show them the Chaperone token and point to the Chaperone player. Put them to sleep. Remove the EVIL NOMINATED reminder.
examples: The Chaperone is in play. The Sleuth nominates the Saboteur and the Prosecutor nominates the Veteran. Tonight, the Prosecutor learns which player is the Chaperone.
The Chaperone is in play. The Groundskeeper nominated the Mansel today. Tonight, the Groundskeeper turns evil & dies and no one learns which player is the Chaperone.
The Chaperone is in play. The Doctor, the Merrymaker and the Snob nominated today. Tonight, no one learns which player is the Chaperone.
characters.quote: Miss, it is imperative you stay close to me at all times. Do not stray, do not stare, and most importantly, do not speak unless spoken to.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If only good players nominated today, wake a good player. Show them the Chaperone token and point to the Chaperone.

characters.name: Paranoiac
characters.ability: The 1st time the Demon kills you, a Minion dies instead (if able).
characters.lede: The Paranoiac can survive getting killed in their sleep and kill a Minion instead.
summaryBullets: The Paranoiac only lives and kills a Minion when attacked by a Demon. Being executed or killed some other way does not count.
If the Paranoiac is chosen the first time, they don't die.
The Paranoiac needs to be able to die for their ability to trigger. If they are protected by the Merrymaker or saved by the Doctor, their ability does not go off.
The Paranoiac's ability must target a living Minion.
If there are no Minions who could die due to the Paranoiac's ability (because they're all dead or protected), the Paranoiac dies even if this is the first time they are attacked by the Demon.
If the Paranoiac kills a Minion, that kill counts as a death caused by the Paranoiac ability and is no longer a Demon kill.
howToRun: If the Paranoiac was chosen by the Demon for the first time, don't place the Demon's DEAD reminder and instead place the Paranoiac's DEAD reminder next to a Minion.
examples: During the third night, the Demon chooses the Paranoiac. The Paranoiac lives and the Nightmare dies instead.
During the second night, the Countess chooses to kill the Paranoiac. The Paranoiac dies.
characters.quote: What was that? I swear I heard the door shut! Who's there?! Show yourself!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Demon chose the Paranoiac for the first time tonight (and a Minion lives), a Minion dies instead.

characters.name: Veteran
characters.ability: You start knowing a player: if they nominate, tonight, a player might die, even if you're dead. If they die, learn another.
characters.lede: The Veteran might kill players if a player they're watching nominates.
summaryBullets: During the first night, the Veteran learns a player. If that player nominates, during the following night, a player might die.
Any player might die, even the Veteran or their chosen player.
If a player dies is entirely up to the Storyteller's discretion.
If the learned player dies, the Veteran learns a new player. There are no restrictions on which player the Veteran can learn.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Veteran and show them a player. Mark that player with the WATCHED reminder. If that player nominates, mark them with the NOMINATED reminder. That night, you may choose to kill a player using the Veteran's ability. If you do, mark that player with the DEAD reminder.
If the player marked with the WATCHED reminder dies, wake the Veteran and show them a new player. Mark that player with the WATCHED reminder.
examples: During the first night, the Veteran learns the Prosecutor. During the day, the Prosecutor nominates. That night, the Chaperone dies.
During the first night, the Veteran learns the Patrolman. During the 4th day, the Patrolman nominates. That night, no one dies.
During the first night, the Veteran learns the Groundskeeper. The next day, the Groundskeeper nominates and is later executed. That night, the Chaperone dies and the Veteran learns the Occultist.
tips: The Veteran kill is a punishment. Don't be afraid to let the good team feel the pain of recklessly nominating. However, don't use the ability if it would bring the good team into an unwinnable position.
characters.quote: August 12, 1874. Thirteen hundred hours. We were surrounded on both sides by the Spanish and the French. My men had already given up hope. We would have died then and there, were it not for my ingenious plan!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the player learned by the Veteran nominated today, a player might die tonight. If the player died today or tonight (including due to the Veteran's ability), the Veteran learns a new player.

characters.name: Spinster
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a living player (not yourself): tonight, if the Demon kills them, you die too.
characters.lede: The Spinster dies too if the player who hosts them for the night passes.
summaryBullets: Each night except the first, the Spinster chooses an alive player. If the Demon kills that player, the Spinster dies as well.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Spinster. The Spinster points at any player. Mark the chosen player with the CHOSEN reminder. Put the Spinster to sleep.
If the chosen player dies tonight, mark the Spinster with the DEAD reminder. Announce their death at dawn.
examples: The Spinster chose the Countess. The Countess is killed by the Guvna. The Spinster dies as well.
The Spinster chose the Socialite. The Socialite is killed by the Nightmare. The Spinster doesn't die.
The Spinster chooses the Prosecutor. The Maiden is killed by the Noster, who then also chooses the Prosecutor. The Spinster dies as well.
characters.quote: Lost is my quiet for ever, lost is life’s happiest part; lost all my tender endeavour to touch an insensible heart.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Spinster chooses a player. If that player dies at any point in the night, the Spinster dies as well.

characters.name: Spirit
characters.ability: If you die, you might register as alive.
characters.lede: The Spirit can appear alive to town and end the game earlier than expected.
summaryBullets: If the Spirit dies, the Storyteller can decide to have them register as alive to the game. If they do, the Spirit may still nominate and vote as normal.

The Spirit should create uncertainty when it comes to knowing how many players are still alive. For game end conditions they should always be treated as dead, so if three players live and one of them is actually the dead Spirit, the game is over.

A dead Spirit can register as alive or dead at any point and differently to different abilities simultaneously, but their state should remain consistent and believable at any time their state is known.
howToRun: If the Spirit dies, you may decide to have them register as alive. While they register as alive, they can nominate and vote as normal. Don't count them as alive for game end conditions.
examples: The Lady kills the Spirit. They die. The next morning, the Storyteller announces that no one died in the night.
The Spirit is dead but registers as alive. They nominate and vote for the Countess.

The Spirit is dead but registers as alive. Four other players live. A player other than the Demon is executed and the Demon kills a player during the night. The game is over because only two players live.
tips: Make the survival believable for the script. In Charged Dinner, there is no execution survival; it is therefore advised to have the Spirit die if executed and not to resurrect them at some point during the game, although these are technically possible.
characters.quote: Honestly, I think the transparency is a perk.
characters.creator: malvora.

characters.name: Maiden
characters.ability: If you died today or tonight, all Townsfolk are drunk until tomorrow dusk.
characters.lede: The Maiden, when they die, causes the whole town to be drunk for one night.
summaryBullets: The Maiden's drunkenness triggers immediately, not at its point in the night order. If they were executed, characters like the Countess or the Doctor are also drunk.
howToRun: If the Maiden dies, mark the Maiden with the FEAST reminder. All Townsfolk are drunk until the next dusk. The Maiden does not lose this ability when dead.
examples: The Maiden died today and all Townsfolk are drunk. The Demon kills the Occultist who has not chosen a Demon. The Occultist learns a "yes".
The Maiden died today and all Townsfolk are drunk. The Demon kills the Paranoiac, who dies.
The Doctor is in play and chooses to use their ability. The Demon chooses the Maiden. The Maiden doesn't die and no one is drunk.
characters.quote: These flowers are right pretty, wouldn'tcha say so too? My papa always says I'm a right pretty flower myself. Though, I ain't too sure about that.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Maiden died today, all Townsfolk are drunk tonight.

characters.name: Nightmare
characters.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player: they die. For each player you kill, a good player learns a player who is not the Demon.
characters.lede: The Nightmare can kill players each night - at a cost.
summaryBullets: On each night except the first, the Nightmare can decide to choose a player to kill. If the Nightmare's ability is then responsible for the death of that player, a good player learns a player who is not the Demon.
Any good player may learn a non-Demon player, even the player the Nightmare killed.

If the Nightmare kills the Spirit, the Storyteller may both choose whether to register the Spirit's death to the Nightmare ability and whether to announce the Spirit's death during the day separately.
If the Nightmare dies due to their own ability, no good player learns a non-Demon player, because the Nightmare ability is no longer active.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Nightmare. The Nightmare either points at any player or shakes their head. Put the Nightmare to sleep. A player chosen by the Nightmare dies - put the Nightmare's DEAD reminder by the chosen player's character token in the Grimoire and put a shroud on it.
If the chosen player died, wake a good player. Show them the THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU and Nightmare character tokens and point at a non-Demon player. Put the good player to sleep.
examples: The Nightmare wakes and chooses the Veteran. The Veteran dies. The Storyteller wakes the Socialite and tells them that the Anomaly is not the Demon.
The Nightmare wakes and chooses not to use their ability. The Storyteller puts them to sleep.
The Nightmare wakes and chooses the Paranoiac. The Paranoiac dies, and does not kill a Minion.

The Nightmare wakes and chooses the Spirit. The Spirit dies. The Storyteller wakes the Anomaly and tells them the Nightmare is not the Demon. In the morning, the Storyteller doesn't announce the Spirit's death.
characters.quote: What was it? Spiders? The Dark? Abandonment? No matter, I'm sure if we try all of them, we'll hit the right one in due time.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Nightmare might choose a player. If the chosen player died, wake a good player and show them a non-Demon player.

characters.name: Saboteur
characters.ability: Each day, the 1st execution you vote for fails. If 4 or fewer players live, you lose this ability.
characters.lede: The Saboteur keeps players from being executed.
summaryBullets: Each day, the first time the Saboteur votes for an execution, the vote tally for that execution counts as zero.
The Saboteur's sabotage lasts only for one day, but the Saboteur may vote for the same player again and again each day.
As soon as four or fewer players are left alive, the Saboteur loses their ability.
howToRun: Each day, the first time the Saboteur votes for an execution, mark that player with the SABOTAGED reminder. The vote tally for that nomination is 0.
examples: There are 12 alive players. The Saboteur votes for the Merrymaker. The Merrymaker gets 8 votes. The Inquisitor also gets nominated and gets 6 votes. At the end of the day, the Inquisitor is executed and dies.
There are 10 alive players. The Saboteur votes for the Maiden. The Maiden gets 5 votes. No one else gets enough votes. No one is executed that day.
The Saboteur votes for the exile of a Traveller. The Traveller is exiled, because abilities do not affect exiles.
tips: You may declare that a zero-tally vote is successful but secretly keep a record of which player is really about to die by marking them with the Saboteur's ABOUT TO DIE reminder, then execute them when nominations are over.

In asynchronous online text games ("longtext"), the Saboteur can easily become outed due to the availability of perfect voting information. You may choose to give the Saboteur a way to more selectively use their ability (e.g. choose to turn their ability off for a day) in order to make them less easily found out.
characters.quote: Cheap rope. Low thread-count, easily tampered with. It's a surprise anyone dies by hanging around here.
characters.creator: malvora.

characters.name: Curfew
characters.ability: Each day, the Xth good nominator is executed immediately. Each night, choose X (>2). You register as good to this ability.
characters.lede: The Curfew cuts days short.
summaryBullets: During the night, the Curfew chooses a number that is greater than 2. The next day, when that many nominations have been made by good players, the last good player to nominate is immediately executed.
The Curfew registers as good to both parts of this ability. They can increase the counter by nominating and they can be executed by their own ability.
If the Curfew enters play, they get to choose a number immediately, regardless of night order.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Curfew. They choose a number greater than 2. Mark them with the appropriate reminder.
During the day, as soon as the Xth good player nominates, announce that they are executed immediately and end the day.
examples: During the night, the Curfew chooses 3. The next day, the Socialite nominates, then the Patrolman and then the Spinster. The Spinster is immediately executed and dies.
During the night, the Curfew chooses 4. The next day, the Chaperone, Prosecutor and Merrymaker nominate. Then, the Snob nominates. Then, the Anomaly nominates and is executed immediately.
During the night, the Curfew chooses 3. The next day, the Inquisitor and the Curfew themselves nominate. Then, the Groundskeeper nominates and is executed and dies.
characters.quote: That's it, no more Xes for you, big fella! Now, get out of my establishment or I'll give you what for!
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Curfew chooses a number greater than 2.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Curfew chooses a number greater than 2.

characters.name: Snob
characters.ability: If an Outsider died today, a Minion may choose to become a not-in-play Minion of their choice. [+1 Outsider]
characters.lede: The Snob can shuffle the evil team around if an Outsider dies.
summaryBullets: If an Outsider dies during the day, for any reason, a Minion may choose to become a different, not-in-play Minion of their choice that night.
Which Minion gets offered to change characters is up to the Storyteller.
Minions may refuse to change character.
howToRun: While setting up the game, remove any Townsfolk character token and add any Outsider character token. This Outsider token goes into the bag instead of the Townsfolk token.

If an Outsider died during the day, wake a Minion of your choice at your earliest convenience. Show them the THIS CHARACTER HAS SELECTED YOU and Snob tokens. The Minion may shake their head no or point at a Minion character. If that character is already in play, prompt them to choose again. If not, put them to sleep and replace their character token in the Grimoire with their chosen character token.
examples: The Maiden died today. That night, the Snob is offered to change characters. They choose to become the Nightmare.
The Veteran was killed by the Demon tonight. No one is offered to change characters.
The Spinster died today. The Nightmare is offered to change characters. They refuse.
characters.quote: Ohhhhhmygod, did you see what Janet was wearing??? Where did she get dressed, the dumpster?
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: If an Outsider died today, a Minion may choose to become a different not-in-play Minion of their choice.

characters.name: The Lady
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Townsfolk you nominate are poisoned.
characters.lede: The Lady can disarm her most dangerous threats by poisoning them through her nomination.
summaryBullets: Each night except the first, the Lady gets to choose a player to die. During the day, the Lady poisons any Townsfolk she nominates.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Lady. The Lady points at any player. Put the Lady to sleep. The chosen player dies—put the Lady's DEAD reminder by the chosen player's character token in the Grimoire and put a shroud on it.
If the Lady nominates a Townsfolk, mark them with the POISONED reminder.
examples: The Lady nominates the Merrymaker who chose the Socialite and the Spinster during the day. That night, she chooses the Socialite. The Socialite dies.
The Lady nominates the Occultist. That night, the Occultist chooses the Lady and later dies. They learn a no.
The Lady nominates the Maiden who is executed and dies. That night, all Townsfolk are drunk.
characters.quote: It's been a pleasure being your host this wonderful evening! Ah, lest I forget, we should all have a toast! You know, to celebrate!
characters.creator: malvora.

characters.name: Guvna
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. A Minion's Townsfolk neighbor is poisoned & might register as evil & as a Minion.
characters.lede: The Guvna makes it harder to find its Minions.
summaryBullets: Each night except the first, the Guvna gets to choose a player to die. A Townsfolk player neighboring a Minion is poisoned and might misregister as evil and as a Minion.
The Guvna's poison may skip over itself or an Outsider to poison a player who does not directly neighbor a Minion, though it is advised that this only be done if not otherwise possible.
The player who is poisoned and the player who might register as evil must be the same, the ability cannot be split up to affect two different players.
howToRun: While setting up the game, choose a Townsfolk who neighbors a Minion and mark them with the POISONED reminder.
Each night except the first, wake the Guvna. They point at a player. Mark their choice with the DEAD reminder. Put the Guvna to sleep.
examples: The Socialite, who neighbors the Curfew, is poisoned. The second night, the Guvna chooses the Paranoiac, who lives and instead kills the Socialite who registers as a Minion.
The Snob neighbors the Spirit and the Guvna. The Guvna neighbors the Merrymaker. The Merrymaker is poisoned & might register as evil, because the Guvna can only poison Townsfolk.
characters.quote: The streets are bursting with the poor, sick and homeless! Others might say this calls for swift action to end poverty! But I suggest: Why not simply end the poor?
characters.creator: malvora.

characters.name: Mansel
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The 1st good player to nominate you turns evil at dusk & only they die that night.
characters.lede: The Mansel makes the first player to cast suspicion on them join their ranks.
summaryBullets: Each night except the first, the Mansel gets to choose a player to die. The first time they are nominated by a good player, that player becomes evil.
If a player is turned evil by the Mansel, they die that night. No one else can die that night, no matter by whose ability.

The first good player to nominate the Mansel turns evil at dusk, right after the day's execution. If the Mansel is executed and dies on the same day they are nominated the first time, the player who nominated them remains good and wins.
An evil player nominating the Mansel does not use up their ability.
If the first good player to nominate the Mansel dies before dusk, they still turn evil and no one dies that night.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Mansel. The Mansel points at any player. Put the Mansel to sleep. The chosen player dies—put the Mansel's DEAD reminder by the chosen player's character token in the Grimoire and put a shroud on it.

The first time the Mansel is nominated by a good player, mark that player with the TURNS EVIL reminder. That night, wake them and show them the YOU ARE token and a thumbs down. Put them to sleep. Mark the now evil player with the DEAD reminder. Mark the Mansel with the USED ABILITY reminder. If any other player should die tonight, do not mark them with a DEAD reminder and do not place a death shroud on them.
examples: The Prosecutor nominates the Mansel. That night, they turn evil and die.
The Saboteur nominates the Mansel. That night, they don't turn evil because they are already evil. The next day, the Patrolman nominates the Mansel. They turn evil and die that night.

The Paranoiac nominates the Mansel. That night, they turn evil. Even though the Paranoiac is then killed by the Demon, since no one but the Paranoiac can die tonight (including Minions), the Paranoiac dies. The Countess also uses their ability on the Snob. The Snob does not die.
characters.quote: One Our Father, three Hail Marys. Oh, and a little favor. One I trust you will keep... confidential.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Mansel chooses a player. If the Mansel turned a good player evil today, that player dies instead & no one else can die tonight.

characters.name: Noster
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Once per night, if you choose a Minion or Outsider, act again. [+1 or -1 Outsider]
characters.lede: The Noster can kill multiple times if it kills Outsiders or sacrifices its Minions.
summaryBullets: Each night except the first, the Noster gets to choose a player to die. Once each night, if that player is a Minion or Outsider, they get to choose again.
The first player does not have to die for the Noster to get to choose again. As long as they are a Minion or Outsider, they get to make another choice.
If the Noster is in play, this adds or removes one Outsider from play.
howToRun: While setting up the game, before putting the character tokens in the bag, either remove one Townsfolk and add one Outsider or remove one Outsider and add one Townsfolk.

Each night except the first, wake the Noster. The Noster points at any player. If that player is a Minion or Outsider, prompt them to choose again. Put the Noster to sleep. The chosen players die—put the Noster's DEAD reminders by the chosen players' character tokens in the Grimoire and put a shroud on it.
examples: The Noster chooses the Socialite. They die and the Noster goes back to sleep.
The Noster chooses the Snob. They get to choose again and choose the Groundskeeper. Both die.

The Noster chooses the Maiden who is protected by the Merrymaker. The Maiden does not die, but the Noster gets to choose again and chooses the Veteran, who dies. They don't get to choose a third time.
characters.quote: Fear not... the beast is sacrificed, yet its essence breathes on. While its suffering was real—you will see it again.
characters.creator: malvora.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Noster chooses a player. If the player is an Outsider or Minion, they get to choose another.

characters.name: Philanthropist
characters.ability: Dead players who vote with you don't lose their vote tokens.
characters.lede: The Philanthropist gives away free votes.
summaryBullets: Whenever the Philanthropist votes, if a dead player who still has their vote token also votes, they do not lose that vote token once the votes have been tallied.
Dead players without a vote token may not vote, even if the Philanthropist is also voting.

If the Philanthropist indicates they are going to vote (for example by raising their hand before their vote is counted) but then does not actually vote, dead players who voted use up their vote token.
howToRun: If the Philanthropist votes for an execution, any dead players who also voted do not lose their ghost vote and do not have to flip over their vote token.
examples: The Philanthropist votes for a player that two living and two dead players voted for. The dead players keep their vote tokens.

The Philanthropist tells a dead player they are going to vote for the current nominee and raises their hand. The dead player votes too, but shortly before their vote is counted, the Philanthropist lowers their hand. The dead player loses their ghost vote.
characters.quote: And you get a knife! And you get a knife! And you! And you! And you! You! You!
characters.creator: malvora.
